quizName: Hardest Questions in Texas Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of having an accident?

options.text: Try to blend in with traffic so other drivers do not notice you.
Do not use turn signals unless you are driving at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Drive very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Tell them what you are doing with your turn signals and brake lights. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Look ahead 12 seconds and be ready to react to dangers.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. Good protective gear includes a sturdy jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: When riding, the best gear to wear is:
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. The best choice is a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider become more visible?
questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright clothing with reflective material. Keep your headlight on at all times. Use your turn signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: What does wearing goggles protect?

options.text: As much as a face shield does.
The same as a windshield does.

questions.explanation: Goggles only protect your eyes. A face shield protects your whole face and is better than goggles. A windshield does not provide enough protection and is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Your friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads instead.

questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have been drinking. Stop them any way you can, including taking their keys. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. What should you do?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.
Wear bright clothing all the time.
Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.
Wear dark clothing all the time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing all the time.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright clothing when riding so other drivers can see you, even during the day.

questions.question: What reduces head and neck injuries?
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet greatly reduces head and neck injuries. A helmet is the best protection a rider has in case of an accident.

questions.question: When your turn is obvious to other drivers, should you use a turn signal?

options.text: No, you do not need a turn signal.
Yes, you should always use a turn signal.
Only if there are pedestrians nearby.
Only if you are at a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you should always use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Use it even if you think your plan is obvious. Other vehicles may be near you that you cannot see.

questions.question: What should a helmet be certified by for maximum protection?
questions.explanation: For maximum protection, use a motorcycle helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Can make a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear when riding.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.explanation: You should wear a long-sleeved jacket made of leather when riding. Leather jackets protect you in a crash. In warm weather, leather also helps protect you from dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool even in hot weather.

questions.question: When using a motorcycle you do not know well, you should:

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good riding condition.
Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
Ride as you usually do, since most bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Be very careful when using an unfamiliar bike. Get familiar with it before you ride. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times to learn the gear pattern.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Hide your intentions from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see others and be seen.
Keep you close to the road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It also helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your lane position should discourage others from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, wear clothes that:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Cover your arms completely, but leave your legs exposed.
Cover your legs completely, but leave your arms exposed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that completely cover your arms and legs to stay protected while riding.

questions.question: The only way to remove alcohol from your body is through:
questions.explanation: Your body must have time to remove alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep going and hope to wake up.

questions.explanation: Do not ride when tired. On long trips, take a rest break every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: For the best protection, make sure your helmet:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious defects.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are slippery surfaces. Ride with extra care on these surfaces.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers provide poor traction. Dry pavement is safer for motorcyclists than these surfaces.
